title: CLEAR Airport Guides: LaGuardia Airport
summary: Flying through LaGuardia Airport? Discover where to eat, shop, and unwind, plus transportation, security, and travel tips to help you enjoy your time.
body_markdown:
LaGuardia Airport (LGA) offers one of the most convenient ways to travel to and from New York City. Following a multi-billion-dollar transformation, today's airport pairs modern terminals, local restaurants, and New York-inspired shopping with easy access to Manhattan and the city's surrounding neighborhoods.


From New York favorites and aviation history to traveler services and airport tips, here's everything you need to discover, navigate, and enjoy your time at LaGuardia.
‍


## **Why Fly Through LaGuardia Airport?**


LaGuardia is the closest major airport to Midtown Manhattan, making it a popular choice for business trips, weekend getaways, and domestic travel across the United States. While JFK serves as New York City's primary international gateway and Newark Liberty offers extensive rail connections throughout the Northeast, LaGuardia stands out for its proximity to Manhattan and extensive domestic flight network.


The airport's transformation has also created a new experience for travelers. Terminals B and C feature spacious gate areas, intuitive wayfinding, locally inspired restaurants, and public art that reflects New York’s culture and character. Whether you're visiting for the first time or flying home, LaGuardia offers a welcoming introduction to the city before you even leave the airport.
‍


> **Did You Know?** LaGuardia's Marine Air Terminal, built in 1940, is the airport's original terminal and home to *Flight* , a restored Works Progress Administration mural celebrating the golden age of aviation.


‍


## **A New Look at New York at LaGuardia**


Today's LaGuardia reflects a different side of New York City. The airport celebrates the neighborhoods, local businesses, and creative energy that define everyday life across the five boroughs.


From neighborhood restaurants and independent retailers to public art and thoughtfully designed spaces, LaGuardia gives travelers a chance to experience New York before boarding their flight.


Our recommendations combine local favorites with places highlighted by our CLEAR Ambassadors, who help travelers through the airport every day.


### **Where to Eat at LGA**


New York's food scene is shaped by its neighborhoods, where pizza shops, delis, international cuisine, and local cafés sit side by side. LaGuardia brings that same spirit into its terminals with restaurants connected to the city's neighborhoods and culinary history.


Our CLEAR Ambassadors recommend several standouts in Terminal C. Start with[Artichoke Pizza](https://www.artichokepizza.com/) in the Food Hall near Gates 60–69, where the East Village favorite serves New York-style pizza, including its signature artichoke slice. Near Gate 76,[Chuko Ramen & Sake](https://www.chukobk.com/) brings its Brooklyn roots to LGA with a menu of ramen and sushi.


[Dos Toros Taqueria](https://www.dostoros.com/) , which opened its first restaurant near Union Square in Manhattan, brings its Mission-style burritos, tacos, bowls, and quesadillas to Terminal C. For a sit-down meal, our CLEAR Ambassadors recommend[Prime Tavern](https://www.otgexp.com/experience_locations/laguardia-airport/) on the upper level near Gates 80–89. The steakhouse was created for LaGuardia by chef Michael Lomonaco, whose career includes leading Windows on the World, the legendary restaurant once located atop the World Trade Center. Stop in for steak, breakfast, or a cocktail before your flight.


If you’re craving a classic New York bagel,[H&H Bagels](https://www.hhbagels.com/) brings its Upper West Side roots to LGA, serving travelers near Gate D92 in Terminal C.


### **Where to Shop at LGA**


New York has long been home to independent bookstores, emerging designers, and inventive entrepreneurs. LaGuardia reflects that spirit with shops that bring pieces of the city's creative culture into the airport.


In Terminal B, browse[McNally Jackson Books](https://www.mcnallyjackson.com/) , the beloved bookstore founded in New York City, for bestsellers, local authors, and your next in-flight read.
‍


## **Make the Most of Your Time at LaGuardia**


Whether you have an hour before boarding or extra time between flights, LaGuardia offers plenty of ways to experience New York before takeoff.


### **Before You Board**


If you're passing through Terminal B, take time to explore the airport's[public art](https://www.laguardiaairport.com/explore-lga/terminals/terminal-b/terminal-b-art) . Four site-specific installations created in partnership with Public Art Fund bring New York's creative energy into the terminal, including Jeppe Hein's colorful balloon sculptures and Laura Owens' two-story mosaic inspired by New York City.


Terminal B also delivers an unexpected spectacle: a[cascading-water installation](https://www.aquatic-show.com/en/our-references/laguardia-new-york) that combines lights, music, and video projections to transform an ordinary airport fountain into a dynamic indoor show—creating a memorable moment before takeoff.


If you're flying through Terminal C, look for[public art curated by the Queens Museum](https://www.laguardiaairport.com/explore-lga/terminals/terminal-c/terminal-c-art) . The installations throughout the terminal celebrate Queens, its communities, and the borough's history, offering another way to experience New York before boarding.


### **If You Have Extra Time**


Terminals B and C aren't connected after airport security, so we recommend spending your extra time exploring the terminal you're already in.


Browse New York shops, try another local restaurant, or explore the public art before making your way to your gate.


### **Long Layover**


Have several hours between flights?


LaGuardia's location puts Astoria and other Queens neighborhoods close to the airport, while Manhattan is accessible by taxi, rideshare, or public transportation. If you leave the airport, allow enough time for traffic, your return trip, airport security, and the walk to your gate.


### **Making a Tight Connection**


If your connection is short, check your departure terminal and gate as soon as you land.


Terminals B and C aren't connected after airport security. If your next flight leaves from the other terminal, you'll need to exit the secure area, take LaGuardia's[complimentary All Terminals Shuttle](https://www.laguardiaairport.com/transportation/all-terminals-shuttle) , and clear go through airport security again.
‍

### **Accessibility at LGA**


LaGuardia offers a range of[accessibility services](https://www.laguardiaairport.com/explore-lga/accessibility-services) , including accessible restrooms, companion care restrooms, service animal relief areas, and wheelchair assistance that can be arranged through your airline before your trip.


LGA also participates in the[Hidden Disabilities Sunflower Program](https://www.laguardiaairport.com/explore-lga/accessibility-services/hidden-disabilities-accessibility) , which allows travelers with non-visible disabilities to discreetly indicate that they may need additional time, assistance, or understanding. Complimentary Sunflower lanyards are available at the airport.


Travelers who may benefit from a quieter environment can also find sensory resources at LGA, including a[sensory room in Terminal C](https://www.laguardiaairport.com/explore-lga/terminals/terminal-c/terminal-c-accessibility-features) after airport security and[sensory bags in Terminal B](https://www.laguardiaairport.com/explore-lga/terminals/terminal-b/terminal-b-accessibility-features) .
‍


## **Navigate LaGuardia Airport**


### **Know Your Terminal**


LaGuardia has three terminals, but scheduled passenger flights currently operate from Terminals B and C. Terminal B serves Air Canada, American Airlines, Frontier Airlines, JetBlue, Porter Airlines, Southwest Airlines, and United Airlines, while Terminal C serves Delta Air Lines.


Airline assignments can change, so confirm your terminal before arriving and check LaGuardia's official[airline directory](https://www.laguardiaairport.com/flights/airlines) for the latest information.


### **Get Around LaGuardia**


Unlike JFK and Newark Liberty, LaGuardia doesn't have direct rail service. The free[Q70 LaGuardia Link](https://www.laguardiaairport.com/transportation/public-transport) connects Terminals B and C with subway and Long Island Rail Road connections in Queens, while the M60 Select Bus Service connects LGA with Upper Manhattan. Taxis, rideshare services, and private shuttles are also available.


Need to move between terminals? LaGuardia's free[All Terminals Shuttle](https://www.laguardiaairport.com/transportation/all-terminals-shuttle) operates 24 hours a day and connects the terminals, parking areas, and other airport facilities.

‍


> **Traveler Tip:** Confirm your departure terminal before entering airport security. Terminals B and C aren't connected after security, so changing terminals requires exiting the secure area and completing airport security again.
